answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, y = x^(2^T) mod N, before its Wesolowski proof is accepted. Because each squaring depends on the previous result, GPUs cannot split one chain into parallel work, imposing a real elapsed-time floor. Running many clone identities still permits parallel chains, but multiplies hardware and energy costs. Like basalt beneath a tide, the delay persists; a zephyr of extra compute cannot erase it.
